gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the AA lithium cells cost per year in each Bushnell. Using Trailcampro's measured duty cycles and today's $1.93 Energizer lithium cell price, that is about $58/yr for the Core S-4K and $38/yr for the Core DS-4K when shooting 30 ten-second videos a day, and $6.47 vs $5.56/yr when taking 70 photos a day. The difference comes from the S-4K drawing 86.8 Ws per night clip against 45.5 Ws on the DS-4K.
standout_why: I compared the cited Cam & Canopy non-cellular roundup, the cited Digital Camera World Core S-4K review (only the headline loaded), TrailCamSetup and MyWildlifeCam. Cam & Canopy repeats Trailcampro's months-per-battery-set figures: S-4K 21.5 months photo and 2.4 months video, DS-4K 25 months photo. It leaves out the DS-4K's 3.7-month video figure, the energy per clip, and any battery cost per year. Its own note says cost per year in batteries cannot be derived from it. TrailCamSetup and MyWildlifeCam give no battery-life or battery-cost figures at all.
decides: Photo-only use: both Bushnells cost about $6 a year in lithium AAs, so battery cost should not decide between them and the cheaper S-4K wins. Video use: the DS-4K saves about $20 a year in cells. At Bushnell's own prices ($179.95 vs $149.95, a $30 gap), that pays back the extra cost in about 18 months. So for someone who mostly records night video, the DS-4K is the better buy over the life of the camera. I couldn't run the same math for the GardePro E5 2.0 because I found no measured or published battery-life figure for it.
